instruction: Center the first paragraph in the document, then save the file.

metadata.explanation: Task requires center-aligning the first paragraph (index 0) AND saving the document. The evaluator checks if the first paragraph has CENTER alignment AND if the file was modified (saved) after task execution. Custom getter reads the DOCX file, extracts the alignment of the specified paragraph, and checks the file modification timestamp to verify it was saved.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Evaluator verifies BOTH requirements - (1) center alignment via paragraph format extraction and (2) save operation via file modification timestamp check

Alignment verification is correct: Getter properly extracts paragraph alignment using python-docx library (lines 52-73), correctly converting WD_PARAGRAPH_ALIGNMENT enum to string representations (CENTER, LEFT, RIGHT, JUSTIFY, NONE)

Save verification is implemented: Getter checks file modification time using VM stat command (lines 23-31) and compares against env.start_time (lines 45-50) to verify the file was saved after task execution
Metric logic is correct: Requires BOTH alignment match AND file_modified=True for success (line 25 in metrics/docx.py), which properly enforces both instruction requirements
Expected values are semantically correct: paragraph_index=0 targets the first paragraph, alignment='CENTER' matches the instruction requirement

Minor dependency: Save verification relies on env.start_time attribute being available. If not set, file_modified defaults to False (line 47), which could cause false negatives. However, this is a reasonable assumption for the OSWorld environment infrastructure
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding fallback: If env.start_time is not available, could compare file modification time against task config initialization time or a recorded baseline timestamp
Add error logging: Log when file_mtime cannot be retrieved or env.start_time is missing to help debug false negatives
